title: Mijn buurt, mijn stad
summary: Neighborhood vocab, Dutch address talk, and the postcode format

blocks.title: Around the block
blocks.body: The words for talking about where you live: *straat* (street), *plein* (square), *gracht* (canal), *winkel* (shop), *supermarkt* (supermarket), *buurt* (neighborhood).

blocks.title: Waar woon je?
blocks.body: A Dutch address ends with a **postcode**: four digits plus two letters, like *1017 AB* — always with a space. To say where you live: *ik woon in Amsterdam*, *ik woon in de Pijp*.
blocks.callout: Canal-side Amsterdammers sometimes say *aan de gracht* instead of *in* — a nice detail, not tested today.

blocks.prompt: Which is a correctly formatted Dutch postcode?
blocks.explain: Four digits, a space, two letters: 1017 AB.

blocks.scene: At the café, Daan asks about your neighborhood.

lines.speaker: Daan
lines.nl: Woon je nog in het centrum?
lines.en: Do you still live in the center?

lines.speaker: You
lines.nl: Nee, ik woon nu in de Pijp.
lines.en: No, I live in the Pijp now.

lines.speaker: Daan
lines.nl: Leuke buurt, hoor! Is er een supermarkt dichtbij?
lines.en: Nice neighborhood! Is there a supermarket nearby?

lines.speaker: You
lines.nl: Ja, en een gezellig plein om de hoek.
lines.en: Yes, and a cozy square around the corner.

blocks.prompt: Describe your buurt: your street, the nearest shop or supermarket, and a postcode (real or invented).
starters: Er is een... in mijn buurt
